newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West major power lines cut further to mid-Oct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West major power lines cut further to mid-Oct.

text.p: Power transmissions on the Pacific Intertie, which runs between the U.S. Northwest and Southwest, will be restricted further through October 20, a notice from the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Wednesday.
Southbound use of the lines has already been limited to 65 percent capacity in response to voltage support concerns following a major power outage which hit the Western power grid August 10.

Transmissions on the alternating current (AC) segment have been cut to 3,200 megawatts (MW) from a full capacity of 4,800 MW, while the direct current (DC) line is limited to 2,000 MW of its 3,200 MW capacity.
But transmissions in both directions on the DC line will be further cut to just over 1,900 MW from early Thursday morning and to zero between 0700 and 1700 EDT.
The rate rises to 2,200 MW north-south and to 2,858 MW south-north by late Thursday, but will drop to just over 1,000 MW in both directions between Friday and October 15.
The DC line will be cut to zero between October 15 and 20.
The restrictions are being made so studies of voltage support, chiefly by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, can be conducted, a source at Bonneville said.
The BPA notice also detailed limitations on the AC line starting on Monday, which are being implemented so that Pacific Gas and Electric Co, can carry out maintenance work on insulator strings.
The line will be limited to 2,000 MW north to south and 3,200 MW south to north between 0600 and 1800 PDT Monday and Tuesday.
The AC line will be restricted to 2,800 MW north to south and 2,500 MW south to north on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
